title: Skift Research travel industry research landing page
answer: This is a Skift Research landing page for global travel industry intelligence, covering airlines, hotels, tourism, cruises, startups and technology. Its most useful AI-related point is that artificial intelligence has turned hotel loyalty into a contest on personalization, but there is no one-size-fits-all strategy. Hotels must decide which path suits their needs. The page is brief and does not provide data, examples or methods, so it works as a high-level signpost rather than a detailed evidence source.

sections.body: The source is a landing page at research.skift.com from Skift Research. It presents itself as travel research offering in-depth analysis of the global travel industry, with news, information, data and analysis on airlines, hotels, tourism, cruises, startups, technology and more. The supplied text does not state a publication date. It is a short page rather than a full report, and the only AI-specific content is a brief statement about hotel loyalty and personalization.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: The page describes itself as global travel industry intelligence. It says it provides news, information, data and analysis on airlines, hotels, tourism, cruises, startups, technology and more. The only substantive AI-related passage in the supplied text concerns hotel loyalty. It states that artificial intelligence has turned hotel loyalty into a contest on personalization. It then says there is no one-size-fits-all strategy. Hotels must decide which path is best suited to their needs. The text does not explain what personalization means in this context, what the contest involves, what paths are available, or how hotels should choose between them. It does not name any hotel company, technology vendor, region or customer segment. It does not offer data, case studies, forecasts or methodology. The broader promise of in-depth analysis is not developed in the supplied text. The page therefore gives a high-level position on AI and hotel loyalty rather than a detailed argument or evidence base.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: The source gives no numbers. Its claims are that artificial intelligence has turned hotel loyalty into a contest on personalization, that there is no one-size-fits-all strategy, and that hotels must decide which path is best suited to their needs. It also claims to provide global travel industry intelligence, news, information, data and analysis on airlines, hotels, tourism, cruises, startups, technology and more.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: A reader following AI in hospitality would use this source mainly as a signpost. It identifies Skift Research as a publisher covering travel industry intelligence across airlines, hotels, tourism, cruises, startups and technology. Its AI-specific claim frames hotel loyalty personalization as a strategic choice rather than a single solution. That framing may help a reader think about how hotels approach AI-driven loyalty, but the supplied text does not provide the evidence, examples or metrics needed to compare approaches or assess adoption. It is best treated as a pointer to a research publisher and a high-level prompt about personalization strategy, not as a standalone analysis of AI in hospitality.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Hospitality

sections.body: The supplied text is a landing page with little substance. It does not state a publication date. It does not provide AI implementation or technology spend figures across hotels, airlines or other travel categories. It gives no methodology, data, named examples, definitions or comparisons. It does not explain the personalization contest or the paths hotels might choose. The page appears to be a research publisher's front page, but the text does not state pricing or access terms. It is partial and high level, so it cannot support detailed claims about AI maturity or spending in hospitality.
